job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people mistakenly believe that Mangalyaan was a cheap mission because ISRO used low-quality parts, but this is completely false. In reality, Mangalyaan was cost-effective because of clever engineering, such as using the PSLV rocket instead of the more expensive GSLV, and by using gravity to assist its journey. Unlike missions that land on a planet, Mangalyaan was designed as an orbiter to study the Martian atmosphere and surface from space, never touching the ground. Furthermore, it did not reach Mars instantly; it took nearly ten months to travel through space, with signals taking several minutes to reach Earth. Similarly, people often think Aditya-L1 will land on the Sun, but the Sun is a massive ball of hot plasma, not a solid surface. Aditya-L1 is positioned at the L1 point, a special location where the gravitational forces of the Earth and Sun allow the spacecraft to stay in a stable halo orbit. Because Earth’s atmosphere blocks harmful radiation like UV and X-rays, Aditya-L1 must stay in space to observe the Sun clearly. This mission helps us understand solar activity, which is impossible to study from the ground because our atmosphere acts as a shield against these rays.

items.evidence: In reality, Mangalyaan was cost-effective because of clever engineering, such as using the PSLV rocket instead of the more expensive GSLV, and by using gravity to assist its journey.
items.q: Why was Mangalyaan able to cost less than other Mars missions?
options: Smart design choices kept its expenses low
Cheaper parts were used to save money
A rover was left out to cut costs
It was launched on a GSLV Mk III
items.explain: The passage says clever engineering, like using the PSLV and gravity assist, made it cost-effective, not poor parts.

wrong.why: thinks low cost means low-quality parts
thinks a rover was part of the plan
mixes up the rocket with the costlier GSLV

items.evidence: Unlike missions that land on a planet, Mangalyaan was designed as an orbiter to study the Martian atmosphere and surface from space, never touching the ground.
items.q: Scientists want to study Mars with Mangalyaan. Where will its instruments work from?
options: From the Martian surface on wheels
From the surface, after a soft landing
From the Moon, looking toward Mars
items.explain: Mangalyaan was an orbiter that studied Mars from space and never touched the ground.

wrong.why: thinks it was a Moon mission

items.evidence: Furthermore, it did not reach Mars instantly; it took nearly ten months to travel through space, with signals taking several minutes to reach Earth.
items.q: A scientist sends a command to Mangalyaan. What happens before it is received?
options: Several minutes pass as the signal travels
No time passes, as signals move instantly
Ten months pass while the signal travels
The signal waits until the craft lands
items.explain: Signals took several minutes to reach Earth, so a command is not received instantly.

wrong.why: mixes signal time with the journey time
thinks the craft landed on Mars

items.evidence: Because Earth’s atmosphere blocks harmful radiation like UV and X-rays, Aditya-L1 must stay in space to observe the Sun clearly.
items.q: Why must Aditya-L1 observe the Sun from space and not from the ground?
options: The air blocks UV and X-rays from the Sun
The Sun is too bright for ground cameras
There is no gravity to hold things on Earth
It must land on the Sun to study it
items.explain: Earth's atmosphere blocks UV and X-rays, so the Sun must be observed from space.

wrong.why: picks an everyday reason about brightness
thinks gravity is absent in space
thinks Aditya-L1 will land on the Sun
